# M3: BehaviourLab

Branch `feat/m3-behaviourlab`, worktree `../nt-m3`. Read `STATUS.md` first.
Migration file: `supabase/migrations/20261120000000_behaviourlab.sql`.

## Goal

Researchers create studies, define questionnaires, invite participants who give explicit
consent, collect observations, view aggregate analytics and export pseudonymous data.

**Hard rules:**
- Studies are `synthetic` by default. A study can only be switched to real data when it has a
  non-empty `ethics_approval_ref` (enforced by a database CHECK constraint). The UI says that
  real participant data needs institutional and ethical approval, including applicable Ugandan
  requirements.
- Analytics report associations with uncertainty, and never causation, diagnosis or prediction.

## Checklist

### Schema and RLS (one migration file)
- [x] Tables:
  - `studies` (`owner_id`, `title`, `description`, `synthetic` bool default true,
    `ethics_approval_ref`, a `join_code` that is unique and random, `questionnaire` jsonb, the
    observation schedule as jsonb, `status`, timestamps).
  - `study_members` (`study_id`, `user_id`, role `owner` | `researcher`).
  - `participants` (`id`, `study_id`, `pseudonym` such as `P-7F3K`, `synthetic` bool,

  - `participant_links` (`participant_id`, `user_id`). This is the only table that maps a person

  - `observations` (`participant_id`, `study_id`, `observed_at`, `mood` and `stress` and

- [x] RLS on every table:
  - Researchers (study members) can read their own studies, their participants (pseudonyms

  - A participant can insert and read only their own observations, through `participant_links`,

## Notes

### What was built

- **Migration** (`supabase/migrations/20261120000000_behaviourlab.sql`, previous builder) re-read
  for this milestone. Researchers have no policy on `participant_links`; studies are owner-only
  for update/delete and member-only for read; participants insert and read observations only
  through `current_participant_ids()`, which requires an un-withdrawn consent; consents and links
  are written only by the `join_study` / `withdraw_consent` RPCs; every helper and trigger
  function sets `search_path = ''`. No changes were needed. It has not been applied (rule 3).
- **API** (`api/app/behaviour/`): `POST /behaviour/associations` (Spearman ρ, seeded 1000-resample
  percentile bootstrap CI, p and Holm-adjusted p, n, strength label, `min_n = 10` guard, fixed
  notice, synthetic echo) and `POST /behaviour/summary`. Both require `AuthenticatedUser`.
  The bootstrap resamples whole participants when keys are sent. It runs on exact count tables,
  so 20,000 rows take ~0.2 s (the in-progress version took ~30 s); a test checks the table
  statistics against SciPy. 29 pytest cases.
- **Pure modules** (`src/lib/behaviour/`): zod schemas mirroring the DB checks, versioned consent
  text with SHA-256 hashing (Web Crypto), seeded synthetic generator, CSV with formula-injection
  protection, time-zone helpers, dashboard aggregates and CSV export builder, with Jest tests.
- **Web** (`src/app/(app)/behaviour/`): studies list with create and join-by-code forms;
  `/behaviour/join/[code]` (consent text, required checkbox, server-computed hash, pseudonym);
  `/behaviour/participate/[studyId]` (check-in form, recent check-ins, withdrawal with optional
  deletion); `/behaviour/studies/[studyId]` (totals, seeder, six aggregate views, trigger analysis);
  `.../settings` (questionnaire builder, schedule, ethics-gated synthetic/real switch, delete);
  `.../export` Route Handler (RLS-gated, pseudonyms only, `export_audit` row written before any
  data is sent, `Content-Disposition: attachment`).
- **Docs and tests**: `docs/models/behaviour-associations.md` (six Crossref-resolved DOIs) and
  `e2e/behaviourlab.spec.ts` (not run, per rule 5).

### Deviations

- **Time of day → craving uses Kruskal–Wallis ε², not Spearman ρ.** Four time buckets have no
  meaningful order, so a rank correlation would be arbitrary. ε² comes with the same bootstrap CI,
  p-value, n, strength label and per-bucket means.
- **Holm-adjusted p-values** are returned and shown, because four pairs are tested together.
- **The API never receives pseudonyms.** The Server Action sends an opaque per-request key
  (`k0`, `k1`, …) for the cluster bootstrap.
- **Two citations are `TODO(citation)`.** Holm (1979) and Tomczak & Tomczak (2014) have no
  Crossref record, so they are named but not linked in the model card.
- **Extras:** `preview_study` and `my_participations` RPCs (already in the migration) drive the
  join and participant pages. The owner can delete a study. "Delete generated data" can also
  remove practice joiners, which is needed before a synthetic study can switch to real data.
- **Once-a-day synthetic prompts** fall at a random waking hour, not a fixed time, so time-of-day
  views have data.
- No new dependencies. No shared files were edited apart from `src/lib/api/client.ts`, as the
  brief asks.

### For the orchestrator

- The migration was validated by reading only. If applying it reports errors, they will most likely
  be in the column-level `grant insert/update (...)` on `studies` or the `random_code` default.
- The signed-in E2E tests need the migration applied and, for the analysis step, the API running.
  Each test creates and then deletes its own study.

### Left unchecked

Nothing.

### Review

Independent review on 2026-11-19 of `origin/main...HEAD` (the `chore(build)` commit skipped).

**Verified**
- **Migration, read as Postgres 15+/Supabase would run it.** Every function is created before a
  default, policy or trigger uses it; `gen_random_uuid`, `uuid_send` and `get_byte` are in
  `pg_catalog`, so `search_path = ''` is safe and pgcrypto is not needed. Column-level
  `grant insert/update (...)` on `studies` is valid and leaves `owner_id` (default `auth.uid()`)
  and `join_code` (default `random_code(8)`, executable by `authenticated`) server-controlled.
  Trigger functions need no EXECUTE grant when they fire. Every helper and RPC is revoked from
  `public, anon` and granted to `authenticated` only; all tables are revoked from `anon`.
- **RLS, attacked as a signed-in non-member, researcher and participant.** A non-member cannot
  read or change a study, its members, participants, consents, observations or export log. No
  policy lets a researcher read `participant_links`, and no RPC returns another user's link. A
  participant can insert observations only for their own participant id while consent is active
  and the study is active; the composite foreign key `(participant_id, study_id)` blocks a forged
  `study_id`. Joining twice is blocked by `unique (user_id, study_id)` (a re-join only re-consents
  the same participant). Consents and links are written only by the definer RPCs. The ethics CHECK
  blocks real data without a non-empty reference, and the guard trigger blocks mixing synthetic and
  real participants. Researchers can write only `S-` synthetic participants and their observations,
  in synthetic studies.
- **Server Actions and the export Route Handler** authenticate first, validate with zod, and
  authorize through RLS (`getStudy` returns null for non-members); the participant id comes from
  the caller's own link row, never from the client. The CSV holds pseudonyms only, is
  formula-injection safe, is labelled synthetic per row and in the file name, and is sent only
  after its `export_audit` row is written.
- **Statistics.** Mid-rank Spearman from count tables, tie-corrected Kruskal–Wallis H, ε² = H/(n−1)
  and Holm step-down were checked by hand and against the SciPy test. The cluster bootstrap
  (multinomial weights over participant tables) is correct. Inputs are bounded (20,000 rows,
  0–10 integers, key pattern) and both endpoints require `AuthenticatedUser`.
- **Scientific integrity.** All six DOIs in the model card resolve on Crossref to the cited
  title, authors, journal, volume and pages. Crossref title/author searches for Holm (1979) and
  Tomczak & Tomczak (2014) found no record, so both stay `TODO(citation)`. Association wording,
  the fixed notice, synthetic badges/notices and the no-individual-prediction disclaimer are on
  every BehaviourLab page.
- All checks green after the fixes: `pnpm check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test` (87), `build`, and
  API `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pytest` (29).

**Fixed**
- MEDIUM: `participants_match_study` now takes a `for share` lock on the study row. Before, a
  seeder insert racing a switch to real data could leave synthetic participants in a real study,
  because the foreign-key check takes only a key-share lock.
- MEDIUM (scientific): the model card and the analysis panel now say that p-values (and their Holm
  adjustment) treat repeated check-ins as independent and are therefore too small; the
  participant-level bootstrap interval is the measure to read.

**Left open**
- MEDIUM: join codes are 40 bits (8 of 32 symbols) and `join_study` / `preview_study` have no
  rate limit, so a sustained guessing campaign could eventually join some active study, see its
  title and add junk check-ins (it cannot read anyone's data). Add rate limiting (M5).
- LOW: `export_audit` is advisory. Members can read observations directly through PostgREST
  without an audit row, and can insert audit rows with any `row_count`.
- LOW: the database does not check that `consent_text_hash` matches a known consent version; only
  the Server Action computes it. A direct RPC call can store any well-formed hash.
- LOW: participants writing through PostgREST directly can bypass zod (DB CHECKs still apply), for
  example extra keys in `answers` (≤ 4 KB) or a forged `created_at`; there is no per-participant
  rate limit.
- LOW: `joinStudyAction` finds the joined study by pseudonym, which is unique only within a study;
  a collision across two of one person's studies would link to the wrong participate page.
- LOW: the CSV formula guard does not catch a leading space before `=`.
- LOW (inherent): a researcher who knows when a particular person joined can match that time to a
  participant's `created_at`.

**SQL that may still fail when applied:** none expected. Column-level grants, the `random_code`
default, the regex escapes (`\-` inside brackets is a literal hyphen in AREs) and the plpgsql
variable names were checked for conflicts.

**Checklist:** every box stays ticked; each item was found implemented.
